purpose: Felodipine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Keeping your blood pressure under control helps reduce your risk of heart attacks, strokes, and kidney problems. Your doctor may prescribe it alone or along with other blood pressure medicines.
how_it_works: Your blood vessels have tiny doorways called calcium channels that, when open, cause the vessel walls to tighten and squeeze. Felodipine blocks these doorways so your blood vessels can relax and widen. This makes it easier for your heart to pump blood and brings your blood pressure down.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include flushing or feeling warm in your face, headache, dizziness, and swollen ankles or feet. You may also notice a faster heartbeat, especially when you first start taking it. These effects often get better after the first few weeks.
warnings: Do not crush or chew the tablet — swallow it whole. Avoid eating grapefruit or drinking grapefruit juice while taking this medication, as it can cause too much of the drug to enter your blood and increase side effects. Do not suddenly stop taking felodipine without talking to your doctor first. Tell your doctor if you have liver problems, heart failure, or are pregnant or breastfeeding.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 5 mg taken once daily in the morning. Your doctor may adjust it to between 2.5 mg and 10 mg per day depending on how your blood pressure responds. Always take it at the same time each day, with or without food, but never with grapefruit juice.
